ARABIC — TERMLY EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.

2. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Only memorise without using the language

3. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.

4. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

5. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.

7. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.

8. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.

9. When practising Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational skills.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Conversational skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational skills.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.

10. When practising Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Selective Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
